Voter turnout dipped in midterms, but beat official expectations | date=November 28, 2022 }} }} {{ElectionsMA}} The '''2022 Massachusetts gubernatorial election''' was held on November 8, 2022, to elect the [[governor of Massachusetts]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] former state representative [[Geoff Diehl]], [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] state Attorney General [[Maura Healey]], and [[Libertarian Party of Massachusetts|Libertarian]] Kevin Reed sought to succeed incumbent Governor [[Charlie Baker]], who did not seek re-election after two terms.{{cite news|last1=Platoff|first1=Emma|last2=Stout|first2=Matt|date=December 1, 2021|title=Massachusetts Governor Charlie Baker will not seek reelection|work=[[The Boston Globe]]|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2021/12/01/metro/baker-telling-allies-he-isnt-running-reelection/|access-date=December 1, 2021}}{{cite news|last=Murphy|first=Matt|date=December 1, 2021|title=Baker and Polito to bow out of 2022, sources say|work=[[Telegram & Gazette]]|url=https://www.telegram.com/story/news/politics/state/2021/12/01/charlie-baker-and-karyn-polito-bow-out-2022-sources-say/8820482002/|access-date=December 1, 2021}} This was one of six Republican-held governorships up for election in 2022 in a state carried by [[Joe Biden]] in the [[2020 United States presidential election|2020 presidential election]], and the only race in which the incumbent was retiring despite being eligible for re-election. Primary elections were held on September 6, with Diehl and Healey winning against minimal opposition. Due to Massachusetts's [[Politics of Massachusetts|strong liberal lean]] and Diehl's [[Conservatism in the United States|conservative]] political views, Healey was widely expected to win the election. The election was called for the Democrat shortly after polls closed, with Healey becoming the first woman ever elected governor of Massachusetts{{efn|[[Jane Swift]] served as acting governor from 2001 to 2003 after [[Paul Cellucci]] resigned to become [[United States Ambassador to Canada]]}} and the first openly [[lesbian]] governor to take office.{{efn|[[Tina Kotek]], the [[Governor of Oregon]], was concurrently elected in [[2022 Oregon gubernatorial election|2022]] and is also openly lesbian, but took office after Healey.}}{{Cite web |last=Rakich |first=Nathaniel |date=2022-09-06 |title=Why Massachusetts's Governorship Is The Likeliest To Flip In 2022 |url=https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/massachusetts-governor-2022/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220906103944/https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/massachusetts-governor-2022/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 6, 2022 |access-date=2022-09-07 |website=FiveThirtyEight |language=en-US}} In addition, with the election of [[Kim Driscoll]] as lieutenant governor, Massachusetts became one of the first two states to simultaneously elect women as governor and lieutenant governor, along with [[2022 Arkansas gubernatorial election|Arkansas]]. Arkansas, however, elects the governor in a separate election from the lieutenant governor. Taking 63.7% of the vote, Healey's performance was the strongest of any Democratic gubernatorial candidate in the state since [[Michael Dukakis]] in [[1986 Massachusetts gubernatorial election|1986]], the best performance in Massachusetts history for a non-incumbent Democrat, and the best performance for any non-incumbent since [[Channing Cox]] in [[1920 Massachusetts gubernatorial election|1920]]. Healey received over 1.5 million votes, the most ever received by a Democratic gubernatorial candidate in Massachusetts. This election constituted the largest shift by partisan margin of any 2022 gubernatorial election, swinging from a 33.5 point margin of victory for the Republican in [[2018 Massachusetts gubernatorial election|2018]] to a 29.1 point margin for the Democrat in 2022. Additionally, every county in the state flipped from Republican to Democratic; this was the first gubernatorial election in which every county flipped since the [[2010 Wyoming gubernatorial election|2010 Wyoming election]]. {{TOC limit|3}} == Background == Despite Republican [[Charlie Baker]] winning re-election in 2018,{{cite news |title=Mass.
